newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares fall despite institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares fall despite institutional buying.

text.p: Jordan's stock market fell on Monday despite institutional and portfolio buying undertaken to raise price levels at the end of the first half-year, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.57 percent to 158.66 points in heavy turnover of 3.7 million dinars dominated by large bloc sales.
Large bloc transactions in four banks, Arab Bank, Industrial Bank, Jordan Investment Finance Bank, and Housing Bank accounted for the bulk of trading activity.
Industrial Bank's large bloc deal of 554,250 shares was worth 1.24 million dinars in a transaction which left its price 0.10 dinars lower at 2.25 dinars a share.
Dealers said most of trade appeared to be focused on orders by local portfolios who sought higher closing price levels for a handful of leading stocks for half-year accounting purposes.
"Some porfolios are keen to raise closing prices of some stocks to reflect on half-year budgets," said broker Ibrahim Odeh, of Wataniyeh Financial Services.
But twenty shares fell on Monday and only eleven rose. Another ten were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.32 percent to 80.72 points, 3.21 percent down from the start of the year.
